title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 1981 'Longue Marche' discussion of what became the section conjecture. On the previous page Grothendieck states Conjecture A. For U an anabelian curve over K finitely generated over Q, every section of 1 → π̄ → E_U → Γ_K → 1 is of one of two kinds: it comes from a rational point of U(K), or it comes from a section of a 'cuspidal' extension (2), attached to a K-rational point at infinity i ∈ (X−U)(K), where X is the smooth completion. Passing to the limit over all open U, i.e. to the function field L of U, he considers E_L = Gal(L̄/L) → E_K = Γ_K. He views E_L as a group 'with infinitely many loop subgroups'. The conjecture then says every splitting of E_L → E_K comes from a splitting of an extension of type (2) attached to some x ∈ X(K). These are the decomposition groups of rational points.

This page continues the argument. The conjugacy classes of such splittings group into 'packets' (reading uncertain). Two sections are put in the same packet when the centralizers of their images Γ^0 are conjugate, even if the sections themselves are not conjugate. Packets correspond to points: all sections lying in the decomposition group of x give, essentially, the inertia/decomposition structure at x. So one would obtain a purely group-theoretic description of X(K) from the extension E_L → E_K with kernel π_{L/K} = Gal(L̄/LK̄). Applied to finite extensions K'/K, the same gives X(K'). At the same time one could reconstruct the open curves U = X − I.

Conclusion: the birational structure E_L → E_K is a priori the richest object. It is far more convenient in genus 0 and 1, where X itself is not anabelian. There one must pass to hyperbolic U of type (g,ν) with 2g+ν ≥ 3 in order to break the continuous automorphism group (PGL_2, translations of the elliptic curve). The birational object needs no such choice.

Finally, he notes that the 'modular/model' form of the conjecture (for the curves U) reduces to the birational form, once one adds a lifting statement. That statement, continued on the next page, is: every section of E_U → E_K lifts to a section of E_L → E_K, or at least to a section of E_V → E_K for a smaller open V ⊂ U.
errors: No real mathematical error. The 'packet' description is heuristic. Distinct sections inside the decomposition group of the same point (they differ by the inertia, which is ≅ Ẑ(1)) are non-conjugate but have related centralizers. The precise criterion ('conjugate centralizers') would need care, e.g. centralizers might be trivial or small; it is not checked here.

The reduction of the open-curve form to the birational form, via lifting of sections, is asserted rather than proved. In the modern literature the converse directions are subtle: lifting of sections to the birational group is not automatic and is essentially part of the conjecture.

ideas.what: Recover X(K) (and X(K') for finite K'/K) from the conjugacy classes of sections of Gal(L̄/L) → Γ_K. Sections are grouped by conjugacy of the centralizers of their images, i.e. via decomposition groups of rational points.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983); developed by Koenigsmann (2005), Pop (2010, birational p-adic case), Stix
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983), in Geometric Galois Actions vol. 1; also in the Longue Marche notes generally

ideas.what: The birational version is preferable because it also covers genus 0 and 1, where the complete curve is not anabelian. Removing points (2g+ν ≥ 3) kills the continuous automorphism group.
ideas.modern_name: Birational anabelian geometry for non-hyperbolic curves / section conjecture for P^1 and elliptic curves via function fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck; Koenigsmann for P^1-type local-global results
ideas.where_published: Implicit in the letter to Faltings

ideas.what: The open-curve section conjecture follows from the birational one plus the statement that every section of π_1(U) → Γ_K lifts to Gal(L̄/L) (or to π_1(V) for a smaller open V).
ideas.modern_name: Lifting of sections to the birational Galois group; the 'section conjecture is equivalent to birational SC + lifting' principle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Discussed by Stix (Rational Points and Arithmetic of Fundamental Groups, 2013), Saïdi and others

missed.claim: Early, explicit formulation (1981) of the lifting criterion relating the open-curve and birational section conjectures. It precedes the 1983 letter to Faltings and states explicitly the motivation via genus 0/1.
missed.quote: La forme "modéliste" de la conjecture précédente revient à la forme "birationnelle", quand on précise cette dernière en disant que les scindage de E_U → E_K se remonte en un scindage de E_L → E_K
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it dates Grothendieck's awareness of the birational/open-curve relationship. It is already known in substance in modern treatments (Stix).

deep.surprise_reason: The birational section conjecture and its relation to the lifting of sections are known and attributed to Grothendieck (via the Faltings letter) and later authors. This page is an early draft-level version with some heuristic detail ('packets' of sections via centralizers), not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'se groupent en/dans [-paquets-] paquets', with 'classes de' (?) inserted below, rather than 'de groupes provenant de ... projectifs'. That is: the conjugacy classes of splittings group into packets.
'et en outre ensemble des sous-groupes qui ont des Centr(Γ^0) conjugués' probably reads 'en outre ensemble des scindages qui ont des Centr(Γ^0) conjugués'.
'Donc on obtiendrait aussi' is likely 'Donc on obtiendrait' preceded by 'Donc on obtient'; minor.
'La forme "modéliste"' is uncertain; it could be 'modulaire' (cf. next page 'sous forme modulaire') or 'modélique'.
